abstract: A caller claiming to be from the telephone/internet provider says the victim's IP address has been compromised by hackers; to 'help catch them' the victim is guided to grant remote access and move money overseas via a wire service, while the scammer secretly takes cash advances on the victim's card.
safe_verification_channel: hang up and call the telco on the number from your bill; providers never need remote access or money transfers to fix a hack
red_flags: asks to send money overseas to 'catch hackers'

abstract: A scammer impersonating a well-known bank offers an exclusive term-deposit/investment with strong returns and walks the victim through transferring savings into an account presented as the bank's, over multiple calls, until the full life savings are gone.
safe_verification_channel: verify any investment on the national regulator's register and call the bank on its official number
red_flags: account not in the victim's name

abstract: A caller says the victim's bank account has been hacked and, over repeated calls, coerces them into moving funds into other 'safe' accounts the scammer controls to 'protect' the money.
safe_verification_channel: the number printed on the back of the bank card / the bank's official app
red_flags: move money to a safe account
